events.title: The pinning-field line defect in thermal geometries
events.speaker: Julien Barrat
events.description:
In recent years, conformal bootstrap methods have been extended to settings in which conformal symmetry is broken in a controlled manner. Conformal line defects provide a prominent example, with applications in both condensed-matter physics and holography. Such defects induce a one-dimensional CFT along the line, making them particularly well suited to bootstrap methods. In parallel, thermal bootstrap methods have yielded new results for CFTs at finite temperature in both infinite and finite volume.

In this talk, I will present ongoing work combining defect and finite-temperature bootstrap methods to study two-point functions of operators supported on a conformal line defect wrapping the thermal circle. I will discuss general constraints on these correlators and show that the finite-volume defect problem simplifies drastically compared with its bulk counterpart. Analyticity and thermal periodicity motivate a periodized formulation of the defect OPE, leading to an analytic bootstrap problem.

The framework is then applied to the conformal pinning-field line defect in critical O(N) models. At one loop in the epsilon-expansion, it determines the thermal correlators of the lowest-lying defect scalars up to a finite (and small) number of constants. I will also present a Padé estimate in d=3 for the thermal one-point function of the lowest-lying scalar, providing a concrete benchmark for future thermal bootstrap studies. If time permits, I will discuss the large-N setup and conclude by outlining related future directions.

events.title: Bootstrapping Pion Form Factors at Large N
events.speaker: DIlara Kosva
events.description: We will start by reviewing the program of carving out the space of large N theories by bootstrapping the scattering of pions. Using analyticity, unitarity and Regge boundedness of the 2-?2 pion amplitude, one can derive two-sided bounds on the EFT couplings and identify the allowed regions in the space of theories. One limitation of this system is that the bootstrap is oblivious to the short-distance dynamics of QCD, where perturbation theory applies. A canonical way to include this UV information is to probe the theory with local gauge-invariant operators, whose high-energy behavior is controlled by asymptotic freedom. We will consider a mixed system of the vector-current two-point function, the pion vector form factor, and the pion scattering amplitude. Rigorous bounds can be derived on low-energy coefficients of the form factor, and by inputting perturbative results through the two-point function, one can also obtain bounds on various couplings that are more phenomenological in nature. We will see at the end how the UV input shrinks the space of allowed theories towards where Large N QCD is expected to sit. Based on arXiv:2606.19420.

events.title: N=4 super Yang-Mills in AdS4 across coupling
events.speaker: Maria Nocchi
events.description: Placing a quantum field theory in AdS offers a geometric way to tame the infrared while preserving spacetime symmetry, making it a useful laboratory for connecting gauge dynamics to flat-space scattering. I will consider N=4 super Yang-Mills theory on a fixed AdS4 background, with boundary conditions preserving 3d N=4 supersymmetry and the full SU(N) flavor symmetry. Starting from the microscopic theory, I will derive the tree-level four-point function of the boundary moment-map operators and use it as input for AdS unitarity to reconstruct the correlator at one loop. In the flat-space limit, AdS poles condense into the branch cuts of the four-dimensional gluon S-matrix, while at finite curvature AdS acts as an infrared regulator. The perturbative results also provide a starting point for following the theory across coupling. At weak coupling, the boundary theory is conformal but non-local. Its CFT data can be used as an anchor for a bootstrap toward strong coupling, where we expect the emergence of a local stress tensor, as suggested by the S-dual picture.
